name: Washougal MX Park

soil.notes: Racers and analysts call it the hardest-packed, most slippery dirt of the summer no matter what is hauled in; the track's own promo calls it deep brown loam that is deceptively slick. Crews rip it deep for nationals.

layout.notes: Set in evergreen forest by the Washougal River. Climbs Horsepower Hill and drops back down. Sun-to-shade transitions blind riders and hide ruts.

conditions.dry: Hardens and gets slicker as the sun dries it; scoop tires usually come off.
conditions.late_day: Early moisture makes ruts that set hard later, limiting line changes; clouds keep moisture longer.
conditions.watering_prep: Groomed and watered; ripped deep for nationals.
conditions.seasonal: Seasonal practice/race dates - call first. Pro national each July since 1980 (one year missed).

rider_reports.says: Analyst: hardest-packed dirt of the summer and dries harder through the day; keep mid-corner roll speed and avoid hard mid-corner acceleration; shadows make ruts hard to see.
Analyst: dirt ripped deeper than normal gave early grip; ruts formed wet and set hard in high-90s heat; use the sighting lap to find new lines and rough spots to avoid.

gaps: Soil description conflict between promo (loam) and racers (hardpack)
